limitations_and_boundaries: The study focuses on the retinogeniculate system; findings may not generalize to other CNS regions.
AAV-Crry did not protect synapses in the somatosensory cortex, indicating circuit specificity.
At peak EAE, demyelination, axon/neuron loss, and gliosis were unaffected by AAV-Crry, suggesting synapse loss is a separable feature.
The study does not directly demonstrate alternative complement cascade activation biochemically; it infers from C3 localization without C1q.
Human data are from postmortem tissue with limited sample size and potential confounds.

research_questions.statement: Is complement C3, but not C1q, localized to synapses in demyelinating disease, and does it mediate microglial synapse loss?

provenance.text_excerpt: unlike developmental and other neurodegenerative disease contexts, synapse loss in demyelinating disease is independent of C1q localization to synapses. Instead, our data support the involvement of the alternative complement cascade, which bypasses C1q and works directly through synapse-localized activated C3, to mediate synapse loss.
